fit: random-order meal composition comparison while taking levodopa
assessment: Five of nine reported worse general symptoms after the high-protein breakfast. A pegboard comparison favored the balanced meal at two hours. Trembling is embedded in a qualitative motor-state category and no turkey ingredients were specified.

fit: high-protein formula and usual-allowance diet during levodopa
assessment: A protein formula shortened the medication response in six patients with motor fluctuations. Diets within the reference protein allowance gave no clear change. The available abstract does not give preparation-specific or resting-tremor results.

fit: post-meal blood pressure and composite Parkinson motor symptoms
assessment: After a standardized liquid meal the Parkinson cohort had a blood-pressure drop and worsening in a cumulative motor score. Tremor was pooled with other motor features and the exposure was shared liquid nutrition.

fit: low-protein product crossover and postprandial OFF duration
assessment: The pilot reports 49 versus 79 minutes postprandial OFF, with no separately reported resting-tremor severity. The exposure is a whole-diet comparison rather than a baked-turkey meal.

fit: firsthand report of weaker perceived levodopa benefit after turkey leftovers
assessment: An individual recalled reduced perceived medication effect during repeated turkey snacking. The cooking method, rest tremor, co-exposures and measured absorption were unreported. The quoted timing question is a separate contribution without a turkey outcome.
